steps: In turns one to five, TicketFlow sends each ticket along with the J S O N schema, Claude complies with valid J S O N, and the context is clean.
But tool outputs pile up. By turn fifteen, more than twenty of them sit in the context window, burying the schema.
At turn fifteen, Claude's J S O N comes back missing the priority field. The schema is buried, and this is format drift.
A junior developer suggests lowering the temperature, but you say no. Temperature tunes output randomness, not attention to the schema. It is not the fix.
Instead, you add a validator that checks every output against the schema, every turn. It rejects the turn fifteen output for missing priority.
Next, you prune the stale outputs from turn five, summarize the rest, for example three A P I calls succeeded, and repeat the schema.
Finally, on the next turn the schema is back in focus. Claude returns valid J S O N, and the check passes again.
